fact: The Institut National de la Statistique (INS), the national statistics office, officially launched data.gouv.cd on 2026-02-23, described as the national open data platform of the DRC and framed as part of the Government's vision for transparency; the document names no open data policy, strategy or decree behind it, so it does not tie the portal to a policy.

The Banque Centrale du Congo launched its new website on 14 August 2026, on which the public can consult exchange rates, inflation, interest rates, statistics and economic indicators, and publications; the document does not say the data can be downloaded or give a licence.
The ITIE-RDC data page publishes extractive-sector data for download, including 280 contracts and a beneficial owner table, and offers a public API, as of 23 October 2026.

ITIE-RDC, the DR Congo's extractive industries transparency body, publishes extractive revenue, mining production, mining-rights and contract datasets for download in CSV, Excel and JSON, with a public API.
The national statistics institute INS of the DR Congo runs a statistical portal offering 15 searchable indicators that users can explore and export, the newest dated February 2026.
Pollicy says the DRC open data portal, supported by the AfDB's Open Data for Africa with contributions from the National Statistics Institute, has not been updated recently.
